records.name_as_stated: Banque de France (table line: "Or en dépôt chez la BDF")
records.relation: holds its gold reserves in custody
records.summary: The Banque Centrale de Mauritanie's audited balance-sheet note on gold states that its gold holdings consist principally of gold deposited at the Banque de France, and the note's own breakdown table assigns the entire holding to that one line.
records.detail: Rapport annuel 2025 of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, section V.4 'Notes sur le bilan', Note 2 'Avoirs en or' (p. 218): "Les avoirs en or sont constitués principalement de l'or déposé à la Banque de France." The note's decomposition table carries a single line, "Or en dépôt chez la BDF", of MRU 1,910,755,583 at 31 December 2025 against MRU 1,157,149,570 at 31 December 2024 — that is 100% of the stated total, so the whole holding is placed at the Banque de France. The accompanying characteristics table gives the quantity as 11,125 troy ounces at both dates, valued at the London fixing (USD 4,308/oz at end-2025). BDF is the abbreviation the same report expands elsewhere; the report's own abbreviation list gives BoE for Banque d'Angleterre, which appears nowhere in the gold note.
records.source_title: Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, Rapport annuel 2025, Note 2 « Avoirs en or » (section V.4 Notes sur le bilan, p. 218)
records.quote: Les avoirs en or sont constitués principalement de l'or déposé à la Banque de France.

blanks.note: NOTHING IS PUBLISHED, not a silent document. The Central Bank of Turkmenistan host cbt.tm answers 403 to curl but renders through WebFetch; the site's own navigation has no annual report and no audited financial statements at all. Its only publications entry, 'Neşirler', points to https://www.cbt.tm/tm/journal/journal.html, a bank-news journal ('Bank habarlary'), and 'Arhiw' (https://www.cbt.tm/tm/archive.html) archives site data, exchange rates and precious-metal rates rather than reports. The single PDF served anywhere in the site chrome is Privacy_Policy.pdf. cbt.gov.tm does not resolve through the proxy (CONNECT tunnel 502). So there exists no CBT document of the class that could name a gold custodian; this is a want-of-document blank and should not be recorded as a document read and found silent. Only remaining route: the most recent IMF Article IV consultation for Turkmenistan, which describes reserve assets but will not name a custodian.

NOTHING IS PUBLISHED, not a silent document. www.bankoferitrea.gov.er does not resolve through the proxy (curl: CONNECT tunnel failed, response 502) and WebFetch refuses it as robots_disallowed, so the host could not be read either way. A WebSearch for 'Bank of Eritrea annual report audited financial statements published gold reserves' returned not one Bank of Eritrea document of any kind — only an Eritrea insurance-sector report, World Bank/IndexMundi reserve aggregates, tradingeconomics pages, and the National Bank of ETHIOPIA's statements (nbe.gov.et), which are a different bank. The Bank of Eritrea publishes no annual report and no audited financial statements, and Eritrea has had no Article IV consultation concluded for many years, so there is no document in existence to read. Want-of-document blank, not a silent document.

A DOCUMENT CLASS IS LISTED BUT NO FILE IS SERVED — closer to nothing published than to a silent document. boss.gov.ss loads normally (200, 202 KB). Its page https://boss.gov.ss/financial-statements/ ('Annual Reports & Financial Statements') lists nine documents, 2011-12, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2020, and NOTHING after 2020. Every one of those links is dead: the 2020 and 2019 files (www.boss.gov.ss/an/Annual-Report-Financial-Statement-for-the-year-20XX.pdf) return HTTP 404 with a 125,655-byte HTML error page to curl and fail as client_error to WebFetch; the older /an/ paths (FinancialStatement2015.pdf, AnnualReportandFinancialStatement2017.pdf, AnnualReportandFinancialStatemet2018.pdf) also HEAD 404 text/html. https://boss.gov.ss/publications/ serves no PDF at all. So no Bank of South Sudan audited statements are retrievable from the bank, none is published for any year after 2020, and no document was read that could have been silent. Next route: the Auditor General (South Sudan), already a party on the map, or IMF staff reports on reserve composition, neither of which will name a custodian.

A DOCUMENT IS PUBLISHED, BUT NOT THE CLASS THAT COULD NAME A CUSTODIAN — and no audited statements are published. The Aden bank's host www.cby.gov.ye resets the connection (curl 35), but cby-ye.com (200, 52 KB) and english.cby-ye.com serve. The CBY's publications listing (cby-ye.com/publicationsandcirculars, 2 pages) carries circulars and credit-risk-information-system forms, not reports. The English site publishes a monthly statistical bulletin: 'Monetary and Financial Developments', December 2025 (https://english.cby-ye.com/files/69b90b6854bb2.pdf, 28,485 characters extracted) and September 2025 (.../69381ea532cd5.pdf, 28,673 characters) were both downloaded and grepped in full. Neither contains the word gold anywhere; the only hit for 'vault' is the definition of Currency Issued ('plus the cash held in banks' vaults'). The bulletin's foreign-asset tables report net foreign assets of the CBY with no asset-by-asset composition. No audited financial statements with notes have been published by either the Aden or the Sanaa bank since 2016, so there is no gold note to read. Want-of-document blank at the statements level, plus a read-and-silent blank on the two bulletins named.

NEW DOCUMENT, STATEMENTS LEVEL — this closes the lever round 69 left open. Central Bank of the Republic of Azerbaijan, CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS for the year ended 31 December 2025 (https://uploads.cbar.az/assets/consolidet.pdf, 1.72 MB, 188,458 characters extracted, downloaded in full and grepped). There is no gold asset line and no gold note anywhere in the statements: a case-sensitive search for 'Gold', 'GOLD', 'precious metal' and 'Precious' returns zero hits in the whole document. Lower-case 'gold' occurs twice only, both outside the asset notes — in the statutory-mandate recital ('Maintain and manage the gold and foreign currency reserves in its charge') and in the profit-distribution policy ('revaluation of assets and liabilities in foreign currency and gold at the year end'). The only custody wording in the document is 'IMF Quota and securities held in custody in respect of IMF Quota' and a 'Custodian fee' expense line, neither against gold — exactly the trap the brief names. 'Central Bank's own vaults' appears once, in the Independent Auditors' key-audit-matter on money in circulation (physical control over banknotes), not gold. This is on top of round 69's reading of Annual Report 2025 section 2.4. Confirmed blank on both the annual report and the audited consolidated statements.

Next document to open: Independent-Auditor's-Report-and-Financial-Statement-of-the-National-Bank_2023.pdf (and the 2024 edition) via a route that gets past the 403, then Note on monetary gold plus the foreign-reserves structure section; also note the NBRNM monthly 'Statement of financial position' files carry a gold line but no notes, so they cannot settle the row. If an earlier Rapport annuel itemises a remainder, that remainder would be a second custodian. The whole publication list is now reachable: bcm.mr is an empty 2,568-byte SPA, but its bundle at /assets/index-B9nUG0IK.js exposes the Drupal back end at https://bo.bcm.mr with a public JSON:API (node/page, node/actualites, media/document; note the host 301s to a /fr/ prefix and brackets must be percent-encoded), and files sit under /sites/default/files/<YYYY-MM>/. That unblocks Mauritania for every other row of this map, not just gold.
